description: The first family-F25 arm (DECISIONS.md 9.143): the F24 run stack on a demand where every bound ride trip can actually become a `ride` alternative in plan memory. Three losses between binding and the choice set are repaired together - a partially bound tour now gets a per-trip plan (60,273 WEEKDAY trips), the escort denial is scoped to the escorting subtour rather than the whole day (33,832 trips across 18,403 persons), and the binder passes no longer book the same person-tour as both passenger and driver (17,740 person-tours, 6.94% of all passenger bookings, 15,002 of them driving and being driven on the SAME trip). What the arm must answer, in order. (1) RIDE. It read -42.5% at the F24 gate and its ceiling was never the pairing rule: the question is whether trips that are now IN the choice set are actually SELECTED by co-evolution, which being in plan memory is necessary but not sufficient for. The seeded ride share rose 0.0338 -> 0.0444; if the realised share does not move with it, the loss is in scoring or pairing and not in the demand, which is the next lane. (2) CAR, BIKE and TAXI. Ride's 8.75 pp deficit and the excesses of car (+6.2), bike (+2.9) and taxi (+1.6) very nearly account for one another, so a real ride gain should draw those three down together; if ride rises and nothing falls, the seesaw of 9.139 is not what it looks like. (3) The pt SPLIT, which is what the F24 gate newly exposed: heavy rail +254.7% and bus +38.2% against light rail -56.0%. Nothing in this family touches it, so it is a control - it should read roughly as F24 did, and a large move means the demand rebuild reached further than intended. (4) CONVERGENCE. This is the first arm since family F4 to run a HORIZON rather than stop at a gate, so it is the first that can measure GOAL.md requirement 8: innovation switches off at 240 and the post-cutoff window straddles 250. (5) The awaiting-run measurements the issues name: #93, #96, #94, #98, #108, #107, #82, #131. S2 x WEEKDAY at 25%, 300 iterations, innovation off at 240, gated every 100 iterations under the loop in GOAL.md with the runner's own watcher stopping the hard bar itself (9.137) - in which case the arm closes itself out as `stopped_at_gate` and its reading is citable at its `reached_iteration` (9.143). 25% is the standing directive (user, 1 Sep). Cost: MEASURED, not projected - the F24 arm settled at 325 s an iteration and took 10.4 h to iteration 99, so 300 iterations is ~27 h; this arm carries ~52,000 more seeded plans on WEEKDAY, each scored once early, so the first iterations cost a little more and the steady state should be close. Graph rendering is OFF (9.59). NEVER compare this arm with any run before the F25 boundary: the demand, the plans and the compiled controler are all part of a run's identity (9.127, 9.138, 9.142, 9.143). NOTHING THIS PRODUCES IS A RESULT until its record says `ran_to_last_iteration`.
